Turning the automatic refill off means your card (ending 4720) is never charged again on its own: no more $15 refills, and your campaign only spends from the $18.52 balance already there. Your campaign keeps its $5 a day, so that balance covers about three and a half days before it pauses and waits for you to add money. If you'd rather it stretch to roughly 18 days, I can set $1 a day now. Shall I?

result.title: Set up a new account
result.content:
# Set up a new account
For an account with no brand yet (GET /v1/brands lists none), or a company it does not hold yet. In order, in any chat (WhatsApp too): never send the person to the dashboard for a step. Steps 1 to 6 send nothing and cost cents: pick the obvious answer and say what you picked. Steps 7 and 8 wait for their explicit yes.
0. **Account** (agents): POST /v1/agent-signups/start {email, phone}, read the 6-digit code in that inbox, POST /v1/agent-signups/complete {email, code} → apiKey (Bearer). A key reaching several organizations: send the client's orgId (or a brandId) on every call.
1. **Brand**: POST /v1/brands with {url, name} (name omitted = read from the site), or {name} alone → brandId. No website: PUT /v1/brands/{id}/business-context {content}.
2. **Offer**: POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/proposals {description: what they sell} (up to a minute) → offers. POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/confirm {offers kept, as returned; chosenIndex only when several} → chosenOfferId = the offerId of every next call; never a placeholder in a path (it also readies step 5, like POST /v1/content/preview-email/prepare). Lost: GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers. Then PUT /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/economics with what your user stated (lifetimeRevenueUsd = what ONE paying client is worth to them, destinationUrl, bookingUrl).
3. **Who to reach**: POST /v1/brands/{id}/icp/suggest {offerId} → one sentence, the targetAudience below; your user's words win.
4. **Audiences**: POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} (up to a minute, saves nothing) → segments. POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments kept, as returned} → audience ids. 409 = name exists: GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId=, reuse it.
5. **Show who and what**: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview → real companies and people, free (not_built_yet: again in a minute). POST /v1/content/preview-email {brandId, offerId, audience: targetAudience, recipient: {firstName, lastName, title, companyName}} from one sample person → show it as written; flag any claim your user never made. 402 payment_required = step 7 first.
6. **Campaign to propose**: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId= → the first proactive row from a source a new account has: name and figure as served.
7. **Prepay, after their yes on the amount**: GET /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_status (active = paid; MCP: distribute_prepaid_status). Else POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout {topup_amount_cents ≥ 1000, auto_topup_amount_cents ≥ 1500, auto_topup_threshold_cents ≥ 500} (MCP: distribute_prepay) → url. Only your user pays it; read the status again once they say they paid.
8. **Start, after their yes on the campaign and a cap**: POST /v1/orgs/audiences/portfolio {brandId, offerId, targetAudience} (call again until ready, nothing re-spent), then the launch in `campaigns`.
Before 7, stop and show your user what is ready: brand, offer, who you will reach (a few company names), the email, the campaign and its estimate. Never pay or start on your own.

What cap do you want on the Zenotris campaign: $5 a day like Instirio, or $2 a day so both run off the balance for about a week?

Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences/portfolio. Derives the active audiences (cold split audiences + buying-signal audiences) for a brand + offer from the ICP text the customer validated. Answers once the cold audiences exist (seconds) with status "building"; the buying-signal audiences finish in the background and flip it to "ready". Poll the same POST until ready: a replay of the same brand + offer returns the current set without re-spending. The gateway waits up to 10 minutes upstream. Request + response shapes are owned by human-service; downstream status and body (400, 409, 502) are forwarded verbatim.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/portfolio, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Response: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/portfolio, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged. Its full document: GET /v1/platform/services/human.

brandId.description: A brand of the calling org. Its site must already be readable by brand-service.

offerId.description: Which offer of the brand to pitch. Required by brand-service only when the brand sells several offers.

audience.description: The audience / segment the sample recipient was found in, in plain English. Given to the model as context.

headline.description: The recipient's own one-line professional headline.

companyDomain.description: The recipient's company website or domain.

strategyId.description: Write the example the way a campaign running this play of the cold-email pipe would: a features-service strategy id on `sales-cold-email-outreach|lead_found_to_conversation` (`offer-emails-only` = leads with something given for free, `named-emails-only` = names the brand and pitches it, `blind-emails-only` = never names the brand, asks about the problem first; any other play of the pipe works too). The email is written with the template + model of the workflow that play's campaign would run (its measured best, else the first workflow it allows in the leg ranking). Absent = the best mature cold-email workflow, as before. A strategy with no play on the pipe = 400 `code: UNKNOWN_STRATEGY`.

question.description: The check's question, as the offer states it.

domain.description: The company the checks ran on.

qualification.description: The offer's checks run on the recipient's company, exactly as lead-service serves them for that company (the same shape as a lead's `qualification`): { domain, checks: [{ question, mode ('must_pass' | 'mention'), verdict ('yes' | 'no' | 'unavailable' | 'not_checked'), evidence, reason, screenshotUrl, ... }] }. Forward it verbatim. Rendered to the model in the same "Checks we ran on their company" block as a campaign email (context only). Part of the stored preview's identity: changed results write a new email, the same results are answered from storage. Absent or `checks: []` = the preview is written exactly as without it.

model.description: Resolved model id that wrote the email.

cached.description: true when this brand + recipient was already written and the stored email is returned (nothing billed).

bodyText.description: The first email of the sequence the product would send, as plain text.

headline.description: The recipient's own one-line professional headline.

companyDomain.description: The recipient's company website or domain.

kind.description: Where the reason comes from. prospect: a fact about the recipient or their company (the data sent in `recipient`). brand: a fact about the sender's company, read from its website by brand-service. audience: the segment sent in `audience`. instruction: a writing rule of the email template (greeting, diagnostic question, call to action), not a fact.

text.description: A sentence or clause of bodyText, verbatim.

start.description: Offset of text in bodyText (JS string index): bodyText.slice(start, end) === text.

reason.description: Why this text is there, in one sentence, as reported by the model that wrote the email.

source.description: The exact input: `recipient.<field>`, `check.<n>` (the n-th check of `qualification`), `audience`, `brand.name`, `brand.<extracted field key>` (e.g. brand.customerPainPoints), or `instruction`.

sourceValue.description: The input's actual value as the model received it. null for instruction.

highlights.description: Why each sentence of bodyText exists and which input it rests on, in body order, non-overlapping. Reported by a SECOND completion that reads the finished email (the writing call is the plain /generate call), then checked here: every text is verbatim in bodyText and every source is an input actually sent; anything failing a check is dropped, so a sentence may carry no highlight. null when that second call failed (the email is served anyway) or for a preview stored before highlights existed.

modelAlias.description: The model alias the workflow states (e.g. glm-pro). null on a preview stored before the preview followed the best mature workflow.

promptType.description: The prompt template that wrote the email: the best mature cold-email workflow's, when it was written.

workflowSlug.description: The workflow whose template + model wrote the email (the best mature cold-email workflow at the time). null on a preview stored before the preview followed it.

data.target: COOs and Heads of Operations at B2B services and logistics companies with 200 to 1,000 employees and $20M to $100M in revenue that are actively restructuring workflows to remove operational bottlenecks and manual reporting delays. Also in are the people around them on this: their executive assistants, chiefs of staff, operations advisors and coaches, and the managers of the operations and process teams who do this work. Out are functions with no stake in this purchase, such as marketing, sales, HR and recruiting, legal, finance and accounting, and IT support, even when the person leading them is very senior. People at companies that themselves sell process intelligence, process mining, or operational process discovery and optimization software or consulting are OUT whatever their role, since they would never buy this; a company selling something else stays in, so only real competitors are out.

POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns.summary: Launch a sales funnel as one campaign (brand x offer x sales funnel)
POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns.description:
Proxy to campaign-service POST /sales-funnel-campaigns. A SALES FUNNEL CAMPAIGN (owner 2026-10-10) is brand x offer x sales funnel: it owns one unit (an ordinary campaign) per pipe of the funnel and is run or paused as a whole. Its money is the funnel's caps at billing (GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps); no max budget = held unfunded. The org is the authenticated one. Status and body (with `reason` on a refusal) relayed verbatim. HOW each pipe behaves is fixed by the funnel's plays (`<leg>@<channel>~<strategy id>` in the funnel id; see the Plays tag: tactic, strategy, play on a pipe, a funnel carrying it, a campaign on that funnel). To change a behaviour (for example replies that carry an offer document as an attachment), launch a campaign on a funnel carrying the right play, created with `status: stopped` until the client agrees. Body { brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: ongoing | stopped } forwarded untouched. 201 when created, 200 for an existing identity.

Request body: documented from campaign-service POST /sales-funnel-campaigns, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Response: documented from campaign-service POST /sales-funnel-campaigns, which owns it; the gateway forwards it unchanged. Its full document: GET /v1/platform/services/campaign.
